newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules against Los Angeles in Prop. 218 case.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules against Los Angeles in Prop. 218 case.

text.p: A Los Angeles Superior Court judge ruled on Monday against Los Angeles County in the first court test of California's Proposition 218, a controversial tax reform measure approved last November by the state's voters.

Los Angeles County had asked the judge to validate the continued collection of the county's fire assessment, which brings in an estimated $51.7 million a year. The assessment has been collected for over five years and was expected to be collected for 20 years, the county said.

The county sought the validation in order to continue collection of the assessment, despite the enactment of Proposition 218. It sought insulation from the property-owner approval requirement and other provisions of the tax measure.
But Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Richard Kalustian refused on Monday to grant the county's request.

Even though the county plans to appeal the decision within 30 days to the state Court of Appeal, officials said the ruling sets the stage for the county to place a replacement tax on the ballot for voter approval.

The Los Angeles County decision was expected to have ramifications throughout the state. Many other local governments have similar taxes on the books that could be challenged under Proposition 218, which requires voter approval of an array of taxes, assessments and fees levied by local governments.
